findings.title: Process-completion persistence performs synchronous SQLite durability work on async gateway/exec paths
The shipped /goal command advertises sustained-goal behavior that default production composition cannot activate
Gateway cron polling performs synchronous full-history durable filesystem work on the event loop
Append-only scheduler evidence has a finite hard lifetime in the live timer path
findings.qualification: Later A01 definition/action/migration/import/service/gateway review found no scheduler-history rollover/archive owner; the earlier provisional qualification is resolved.

findings.title: Completed delivery dispatch entries are retained for the lifetime of the outbox store
Model-facing cron list/remove authority is global across chats
findings.qualification: Conditional on mutually untrusted chats/users sharing one agent/service; a strictly single-owner instance may intentionally define one administration domain.

findings.title: Shipped local-trigger commands queue work that the default gateway never consumes
Local-trigger restart recovery can replay an already committed turn and its effects
findings.qualification: Conditional on local-trigger execution being activated; the default foreground gateway does not start the runner.

findings.title: Local-trigger automation can affirm a pending risky-action approval
findings.qualification: Conditional on local-trigger execution being activated; approval admission is source-blind once automation shares the bound session/channel alias.

final_discussion_questions.question: Should process-completion, cron and future trigger durability share one ordered asynchronous persistence-owner pattern while retaining current pre-effect fsync semantics?

What explicit epoch/archive policy should retire scheduler classifications, trigger requests, action receipts, scheduling commits and offline reconciliation evidence without weakening replay/authority proofs?
Is model-facing cron management intentionally instance-global, or should creator/session scope be the default with a separate administrator capability for global list/remove?
Should /goal and local-trigger commands be activated as supported first-party features, or hidden until their required tools/runtime owners are present?

Before local triggers are activated, should each delivery acquire a durable canonical run/settlement identity with explicit committed/unknown/retryable states rather than filesystem at-least-once recovery?

Should risky-action approval consumption be restricted to trusted foreground user ingress, making all cron/trigger/recovery/background automation incapable of affirmative/negative approval settlement?
Which legacy session-bound cron helpers, stale dormant comments and historical retry caches should be retired once the canonical occurrence/outbox path is the only supported owner?

cross_module_dependencies_and_conflicts.dependency: Default tool manifest/registration controls sustained-goal reachability and command/capability consistency.
Session/turn ownership and approval admission affect automation alias and approval authority.
Gateway/channel trust domains affect cron management scope and future trigger activation.
Repository-wide recovery/idempotency policy should reconcile local-trigger crash replay.
Legacy cron helper retirement, feature gating and evidence-retention simplification remain deferred.

additional_observations.text: Cron scheduled execution deliberately requires qualified POSIX descriptor/flock support and fails closed otherwise.
Canonical cron modules still carry stale dormant comments and older session-bound/message-fanout helpers remain as retirement debt.
Delivery/operator reconciliation has explicit finite attempt/evidence bounds distinct from the live scheduler exhaustion finding.
Management action receipts and scheduling commits also have 4,096-item maintenance horizons without a matching cron export owner.
Definition retry caches retain historical full candidate wires until restart; growth is indirectly bounded by durable evidence ceilings.
Negative every_seconds is schema-admitted and reaches typed validation as an exception rather than a normal tool diagnostic.
Local-trigger storage is compatibility-grade pathname/FileLock JSON storage and should be reconsidered before first-party activation.
